initiatives.name: San Francisco Tenants Union
initiatives.description: Member-supported organization fighting for tenants' rights and housing justice through direct support, education, and collective organizing.

initiatives.name: Coalition on Homelessness
initiatives.description: San Francisco group, founded 1987, that organizes unhoused people and service providers for housing and against sweeps and citations; publishes the Street Sheet newspaper.

initiatives.name: Eviction Defense Collaborative
initiatives.description: San Francisco nonprofit providing free legal representation and rental assistance to tenants facing eviction. Runs the city's Tenant Right to Counsel program from 976 Mission St.

initiatives.name: SF Anti-Displacement Coalition
initiatives.description: Coalition of San Francisco tenant organizations and allies organizing against evictions and rent increases. Holds tenant assemblies and free legal clinics.

initiatives.name: San Francisco Food Not Bombs
initiatives.description: Volunteers serve free vegetarian meals in San Francisco on Wednesdays at 16th & Mission and Fridays at 9th St.

initiatives.name: PODER SF
initiatives.description: Organizes Latinx immigrant families and youth in San Francisco's Mission, Excelsior and southeast neighborhoods on environmental and economic justice issues, climate resilience and civic engagement.

initiatives.name: Chinese Progressive Association
initiatives.description: Grassroots organization building collective power with working-class Chinese immigrants through mutual aid, worker and tenant organizing, youth leadership development, and environmental justice initiatives.

initiatives.name: People Power Media
initiatives.description: San Francisco housing justice group that makes popular education media (like the animated short Priced Out), runs workshops, and staffs the REP-SF planning coalition.

initiatives.name: SF Mutual Aid
initiatives.description: A community network coordinating mutual aid efforts and connecting neighbors to share resources across San Francisco through direct support, solidarity, and collective care.

initiatives.name: GLIDE
initiatives.description: Tenderloin social services organization at 330 Ellis St in San Francisco, offering meals, health and recovery services, housing support, and advocacy for people in poverty.

initiatives.name: The Women's Building
initiatives.description: Mission District community center, in its building since 1979, offering a food pantry, legal aid, financial coaching, tax clinics, and job search help for women, immigrants, and LGBTQ+ people.

initiatives.name: Resistance SF
initiatives.description: General protest calendar and community organizing resource.

initiatives.name: Queerious Labs
initiatives.description: Queer art and technology workshop and hackerspace in SoMa, San Francisco, hosting classes, events, and projects like digitizing the On Our Backs archive.

initiatives.name: The Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence
initiatives.description: San Francisco order of queer and trans nuns, active since 1979, doing community service, fundraising grants, and public events, plus a campaign on intimate partner violence.

initiatives.name: Lavender Phoenix
initiatives.description: Bay Area organization (formerly APIENC) of transgender, non-binary, and queer Asian and Pacific Islander people that trains grassroots leaders and runs member organizing programs.

initiatives.name: SF LGBT Center
initiatives.description: Community center at 1800 Market St. in San Francisco offering LGBTQ+ employment, financial, and youth services, plus community programs and events.

initiatives.name: Gay Shame
initiatives.description: Queer and trans activist group in San Francisco, founded in 2001, that protests corporate Pride, gentrification and policing through street actions and theater.

initiatives.name: San Francisco Food Not Bombs
initiatives.description: Mutual aid group providing free vegan food and resources in so-called San Francisco every Wednesday & Friday night .

initiatives.name: harm reduction outreach collective
initiatives.description: SF based peer-led harm reduction

initiatives.name: Silver Sprocket
initiatives.description: Independent comics publisher and art collective in San Francisco that publishes zines, comics and graphic novels. Its Valencia St. shop closed in March 2026; publishing and online sales continue.

initiatives.name: Betti Ono
initiatives.description: Oakland nonprofit led by Black women and survivors, founded 2010; runs artist residencies, youth fellowships, a mobile cultural hub and programs to end gender-based violence.
